jc.t: Blessings at the Sunday assembly: "The mandir is done
w: It will happen here in the future."

In the evening assembly the kishores sang: "Jivan jivi janyu nahi to jindgi shaa kaamni" and presented a performance of historical figures like King Soloman, Alexander the Great, Elvis Prestly, Chanakya and others - each narrating their achievements and the subsequent emptiness and vaccum in their lives. This was followed by a drama presentation of devotees who have been transformed and blessed by Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
At 8.30 am Pramukh Swami Maharaj sat down for breakfast. Some teenagers were sitting in front. Today they had come having made some good resolve.

Each teenager would stand up, first state his resolve and pray to Swamishri or take a vow, and then introduce the teenager sitting next to him. In this way the teenagers stood up one after another. While having breakfast, Swamishri showed great interest in listening to them. These teenagers were eagerly taking vows that are hard to keep in the atmosphere here, such as not watching TV or cinema, going to university with tilak chandlo, doing daily puja regularly even while living in the university hostel, not eating outside food, and so on. These teenagers took such vows firmly! Not only that, some brave teenagers who had gone deeper into satsang went even further. One teenager said, "Bapa! My prayer to you is that dharma, knowledge, detachment and devotion grow in me."
Swamishri said, "Wonderful, you have said the supreme thing!"

Another teenager said, "Bapa! Yesterday you instructed us to bow to our parents, but now I am going to study at university, so I will take a photo of my mother and father with me. I will do panchang pranam (a five-limbed bow) to it every day."
One teenager said, "Bapa, I will regularly read satsang books."
"Bapa! Worldly pleasure is transient. Keep me away from it and give me love for you." One teenager made this prayer too.

Receiving the heartfelt feelings of these teenagers, Swamishri cast a pleased glance on them and said, "Keep your vows firmly. Be brave. Yogi Bapa, whom you have attained, will remove the world from your soul. He will give you love for God. Do not take a step back."

Teenagers were telling Pramukh Swami Maharaj about their experiences. The stories of how firmly the youths keep their vows amid the pleasure-seeking atmosphere of the USA were thrilling. Speaking about some of the hard questions and vows that trouble all the teenagers studying at college and university, Ashwin Patel said, "Bapa! We find it very hard to keep the vow of applying tilak chandlo, yet there are many teenagers who apply tilak chandlo fearlessly.

"Second, if one does not go to eat at restaurants with the other students, friends keep asking, 'Why doesn't he eat with us? Is he upset about something?'... So the vow of not eating outside food is also hard to keep, yet many teenagers keep that vow firmly too.
"Third, please give us guidance on how to keep our satsang firm at this age.

"And fourth, how to balance the mandir and studies is also a big question. When exams are near, the question especially arises whether to go to the mandir or to study. If we stay back to study, we feel sad at missing darshan, the assembly and seva. So our prayer is that you give us strength to balance this."
With the wish that their satsang stay firm even amid such complex questions, all the teenagers sang together the prayer "Dharmakunvar Harikrishnaji tame...".

Swamishri felt like shedding special light on the four questions the teenagers had presented. Saying "Bring the microphone," he asked for it himself and said, "What was the first question? About tilak chandlo. We do not apply tilak chandlo to harm anyone. It does not harm the teacher, the student or anyone. Others may not like the clothes we wear. So what harm does it do them? If others do not like the house we live in, should we abandon the house? This happens with everything. What one person likes another may not, but that does not mean we give the thing up. If others do not like it that you earn more money, do we throw the money away? So that will happen. When we apply tilak chandlo we do not harm anyone. We live our lives according to our customs. Even so, jealous people will be jealous. If you do it they will talk, and if you don't they will talk. We do not apply tilak chandlo to please people. We do not become good because people call us good, and we do not become bad because they call us bad. We do it because God likes it. We do it to please God. When we offer devotion, do satsang, keep vows, do austerities and fasts, others are not going to like it. That is no reason to give it up. Those people want to please society, to please the body. We want to please God, to please the Sant, so we should act according to their wishes, and whatever we have to bear in doing so, we should bear. There is no need to quarrel with them. Everyone keeps the symbol of their own religion. In the same way, this is our religious symbol. Our High Court judges, Supreme Court judges and even the Speaker of Parliament go on duty with their religious symbols. If the mind is firm, there will be no problem.

"The second thing you spoke of was eating outside food. In this country of yours there is the greatest difficulty. Even if it is called vegetarian, it is not vegetarian, because the serving spoon goes from this dish into that one, so things get mixed. So do not eat outside food at all. Prepare it at home and take it. Those living in college hostels should learn to make things like bhakhri and vegetables. Take some ready-made food that your parents prepare for you. In the past, in the gurukul, boys cooked for themselves, washed their own clothes, made their own beds. A self-reliant life. This is for those who want to follow dharma. You have the difficulty of studying and doing this too, but whoever finds it possible, it is good if they do so. Those whose home is nearby should make food at home and take it. When the other boys are eating, eat whatever we have taken. Eat fruit. If you try, it will become manageable. God helps those who have courage.

"In this country people are eating from the moment they get up, and in that, if you think of fasting, it is a great thing, isn't it! It is hard for you. Yet you have satsang, so through the strength of satsang you have this much enthusiasm. If such an occasion comes and you cannot get vegetarian food, then fast for a day. You can get dry fruits, can't you! Eat those. Some people live on juice, on milk. The rishis and munis lived on leaves. In the same way we should manage with such things, but keep our life pure.

"Third, when exams come, keep a firm resolve for two or three months. At that time it does not matter if mandir work is reduced. Do not plan camps at that time either. At that time give more importance to studies. Pay proper attention at the time of final exams. In the rest of the time, we should do satsang activities. Set aside Saturday and Sunday for satsang.
"If coming to the mandir is reduced at exam time, hold an assembly at home. If a ghar sabha cannot be held, do a little reading on your own. One who wants to do it can do everything.

"Everyone, keep up your strength. We want to please God. If that One is pleased, the whole world is pleased. All the deities are pleased... Ballads are written about those who are brave. Bravery means keeping control over the senses and firmly observing one's vows and dharma. Everyone has to keep this bravery."
This generation of teenagers, nurtured by Swamishri with the waters of affection, will become the saviours of the future.

st.t: Special decennial program by Ladies wing, San Jose, CA
w: In 1991 H.D.H. Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated Shree Swaminarayan Mandir, in Milpitas, CA. Ladies Chapter celebrated the event with cultural programs and exhibition - titled "Essence Of The East”. Melodious prayer - bhajans, several Indian classical dances, thought-provoking speech, informative presentations, and humorous plays enchanted the packed audience. Local bay area organizations also presented some items. Themes ranged from “In search of God”, “The importance of Temple”, to contemporary living.

The Kishori Mandal depicted the charm and beauty of an Indian village woman in a graceful dance ballet. The highlight of the day was a breathtaking performance by the Balika Mandal in a series of folk and classical dances titled "Tapestry of Indian dances". It provided a glimpse of the rich culture and diversity of music,language, dance and costumes in India by covering states from the North, East, South and West. A play titled "Chabarda.com", had the entire audience break into laughter. This play portrayed how the Gujarati language can be transformed into a comedy of errors by children who are born and raised here - in America.

All Ladies chapters of BAPS in California, and several other leading socio-religious local organizations supported and participated in this unique event. An informative exhibition focusing on Hinduism was displayed throughout the event. Representatives of more than six spiritual and social organizations graced the occasion. Two local newspapers namely “India West” and “India Post” also covered the event. At the end, mementos were awarded to the participants.
Swamishri performed the murti pratishtha rituals of Shri Akshar Purushottam Maharaj and Guru Parampara for the BAPS residential girls' school - Swaminarayan Vidyapith, Karamsad.
In the morning, the Kishore Day assembly was based on the subject of Niyam Dharma. The assembly was attended by 430 kishores and 180 kishoris.

In the evening, the Children's Day program included a march (kuchh geet) and the demonstration of a children's weekly assembly to show what children are taught. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly.

Yuvak - Yuvati Din After Swamishri had darshan in the mandir, he released balloons to launch today's Yuvak-Yuvati Day, after which yuvaks sang various kirtans during Swamishri's puja. A special morning assembly was arranged for them, in which Doctor Swami addressed them. The highlight of the evening assembly was a drama performed by the yuvaks entitled 'Brahmanand Darshan'.

In his blessings to the assembly, Swamishri first praised the devotion and services of the Yuvak Mandal. He also stressed the importance of discourses in addition to seva, saying that without the understanding and knowledge provided by discourses, ego will come in the way and one will be unable to perfect one's devotion.
Thursday, 28 July 2005 (Ashadh vad 8, Samvat 2061), Bochasan

In the evening, after his walk and yoga postures, when Pramukh Swami Maharaj sat down to take prasad, talk turned to the old sadhus. Govind Swami of Sanjaya did the storeroom work and also served food. He did every kind of seva. He lived in a room of the dharmashala. Another such old sadhu was Mota Akshar Swami, Santda, who was from Sisva. Both these sadhus had left with Shastriji Maharaj. Mota Akshar Swami was very strong. For the mandir there would be a big stone beam, and he would be at one end of the beam and Soma Bhagat at the other, and the two of them would lift it and throw it to one side. That is how strong he was. He was also forgetful by nature. It was the vacation, so I was travelling with them through the villages. We had to go from Shantipura to Nenpur. Prabhudas of Shantipura said, 'Swami! I will harness a damniyu (small bullock cart) for you.'

'We will walk. There is no need. Your farm work is going on now!' Akshar Swami said no, but Prabhuda left his plough and wood and brought the cart. They sat in it. When Nenpur must have been about one gaam (a local measure of distance) away, Akshar Swami said, 'You go now, Nenpur is right here, we will walk.' Govind Swami, who was with him, said, 'We can walk, but this boy is young (Swamishri was speaking about himself), the poor boy will have trouble.'

But Akshar Swami said, 'There will be no problem. We will walk.' Saying this he got down from the cart. Akshar Swami had a bundle on his head. Govind Swami had also taken a bundle. In my hands I had my bag and another bundle too. It was getting dark. We walked. We walked and walked... and reached all the way to the bank of the Vatrak. When we got here, Akshar Swami said, 'Look, we have reached Mehmedabad.' There on the river bank we bathed a little and then came back along the railway tracks, and in that way reached Nenpur. Akshar Swami was that forgetful. His memory was like that, yet when Shastriji Maharaj touched his thumb to his forehead and said, 'Go, you have attained knowledge,' every word of the Vachanamrut came to his lips.
Thursday, 28 July 2005 (Vikram Samvat 2061, Ashadh vad 8), Bochasan

At 7.00 pm Swamishri arrived at the Rariton Expo Centre in Edison for the welcome function. A replica of Akshardham made of polystyrene formed the stage backdrop. Prior to Swamishri’s arrival senior sadhus had addressed the large gathering. On his arrival senior sadhus garlanded Swamishri. Thereafter the Mayor of Edison Hon. Jun Choi honoured Swamishri with a proclamation and declared the day as ‘Pramukh Swami Day’. The Mayor praised the BAPS and Swamishri in his address. Then Swamishri blessed the CEO of TV Asia Shri H.R. Shah and social worker Bharatbhai Shah. Shri H.R. Shah praised Swamishri as today’s sanskruti purush (culture personality). Children and youths performed a cultural dance and a drama on family disputes and miscommunication. Then Shukmuni Swami spoke on effective communication. Finally Swamishri blessed the function, “We are indebted to one’s family, society and country. But our obligation to God is the greatest. Whatever you have achieved, do not use it unethically. Live morally and spiritually and consolidate our cultural values in life. If the foundation of a building is strong then the building will stand for many years. So, one has to take care in constructing the foundation. If one becomes engrossed in material pleasures, the present lifestyles and wealth then one’s foundation will become weak. We must observe and preserve our values of truth, ahimsa, brahmacharya, compassion.” The assembly concluded at 8.30 pm. About 7,000 devotees and well-wishers were served with prasad.
A spiritual seeker from South India said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "What is the way to rise above all three states (waking, dream and deep sleep)?"
Swamishri said, "A firm refuge in God. Turn the mala of God every day and pray."
A seeker from South India said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "What is the way to go beyond all three states (waking, dreaming and deep sleep)?"
Swamishri said, "Firm refuge in Bhagwan. Turn the mala of Bhagwan every day and pray."

Today, after puja, as Mahant Swami Maharaj was taking his medicine, the sadhus showed him the Akshar Deri made of flowers that had been arranged in the puja. Swamishri was looking at the flower decoration. The sadhus said, "This was in the puja."
But no one's devotion escapes Swamishri's notice. Nodding his head in agreement, he said, "It was at the bottom on the left."
Today Dr Rajmayurbhai was on medical seva. Mahant Swami Maharaj called him close and said, "At that time (previously) he was fat; we wondered where he would end up. But he lost it."
Dr Rajmayurbhai said, "Swami! Just as I have improved the outside, please improve the inside."
Swamishri laughed and said, "You are the doctor of the outside (the body) and we are the doctor of the inside (the soul)."
It was as if Swamishri had said that the only thing we know how to cure is the disease of birth and death; we do not know anything else.
On the plane from Toronto to San Jose.

As soon as the plane took off and climbed a little, Mahant Swami Maharaj took Thakorji onto his lap. Turning Harikrishna Maharaj's face towards the window, he began to show him the city of Toronto. As the plane went higher, he supported Thakorji's plate from below with one hand, keeping it slightly tilted, so that Maharaj's gaze would fall on the ground below. For about 15 to 20 minutes, he had Harikrishna Maharaj cast his glance on the houses below in this way.
The devotees asked, "While having Harikrishna Maharaj cast his glance, what were you thinking?"
Swamishri said, "May everyone (below) be happy. May everyone find satsang in their next birth."
What a noble feeling!
Today Mahant Swami Maharaj gave very beautiful blessings in the evening assembly:

"Maharaj came, the Gunatit gurus and Pramukh Swami Maharaj all came and became like us. What if they had not become like us? It is hard to look at even one sun. If the sun came down a little, it would burn everyone to ashes. So how could one look at the light of countless suns? That is why they became completely like us. Nishkulanand Swami wrote: 'Kiya kidi kari melap (bhelo thava) bhare bhed chhe re' (how can an ant meet him; there is a vast difference). Where is Purushottam himself and where are we?

We have attained contact with Bhagwan through the sadhu; this is something to keep firmly fixed in the mind. Now we have the same attainment that there was in Maharaj's time. If we do not understand this, we all go round in circles and get confused. We often wonder what to do in this attainment. The answer is faith. Faith itself is the attainment."
